d: A look at what happened to Custer and his troops at the Battle of Little Big Horn.
A noble cattleman battles an embittered, rival rancher, who hires ten outlaws to seize power in the territory.

Buck Jones, to all appearances a Native American, becomes a Pony Express rider in the period just after the Civil War. Thieving white men, led by Robert Ellis, have been stealing the organization's finest steeds and blaming their encroachments on neighboring Indians. The noble Jones uncovers Ellis' treachery and discovers that he himself is really a white man.

Bill Elliott plays the western legend, Wild Bill Hickok, in this routine adventure about a group of settlers who leave Kansas for a go at the wilderness of Colorado. They come up against a band of Indians who don't want any more white settlers on their land.
A pacifist Civil War veteran resorts to violence to free his fiancée from the clutches of a psychotic gang.
A well-meaning drifter is caught between a ranch owner's unfaithful wife and her husband's jealous foreman.
A cowboy seeks revenge against the double-crossing settler responsible for his fiancée's murder.

Charles Starrett stars as a federal agent assigned to stop the illegal flow of silver from Mexico into the U.S. The lawman soon figures out that the local U.S. attorney, Tristram Coffin, is in cahoots with the smugglers. After a few chases and shootouts, Starrett fulfills his mission.
After a raid by Comanches, six remaining cavalrymen join a stagecoach and lead it to safety.

Charles Starrett is the Durango Kid. He is also the marshal, Steve Allan. When Robert Malcolm, a wealthy old land mogul, is killed, the finger points at Steve Darrell and Gaylord Pendleton, Malcolm's siblings.
A quiet young farmer turns into a deadly gunfighter who dedicates his life to the pursuit of evildoers.
Trappers working as scouts at a remote army fort witness the unprepared garrison attack a sizable Sioux force.
An idealistic Army doctor faces the hostility of his own men when he helps the malaria-stricken Kiowa tribe.
A portrait of the vile and muddy old west and the genesis of Billy the Kid.
A rebellious man and his partner, raise a ruckus in a small town after they rescue a man from a lynching.
A loudmouth cowboy with a history of telling tall tales goes to Hollywood, where his lies catch up to him when he is asked to perform some of his feats.
A jailed rancher escapes to track down the outlaws who framed him for a murder he didn't commit.

The Durango Kid (Charles Starrett) stops a mother (Mira McKinney) and her two sons (Don C. Harvey and Myron Healey) from stealing the ranch lands and gaining control of the valley when it is discovered that an underground rivers runs through the ranches.

The Durango Kid tries to stop a war between Indians and the US Cavalry from escalating. A couple of outlaws disguised as Indian scouts are trying to instigate the war to lay claim to gold that has been discovered on the Indians' land.

Ellis plays a city slicker from Chicago who buys up land to have it developed by one set of tenants, while at the same time the deeds are being sold to someone else back in the city. When the new owners come to stake their claims, trouble erupts. But sheriff Jones settles everything for both parties.
A ruthless landowner uses an attack on a wagon train as an excuse to begin a war that will enable him to claim Apache territory as his own.
A US Marshal is forced to lead a gang of bandits to a hidden valley of gold.
Two brothers on a quest to find their long-lost, kidnapped sister, who now lives as part of an Indian tribe.
A bank heist gone awry leaves a small town in the grip of a band of deadly outlaws.
The Durango Kid comes to Texas with the avowed intention of clearing the name of his father, who has been framed by some crooked politicians and slain.
An ex-soldier's plans to move east are delayed after his brother is murdered on the orders of a land baron.
Four brothers, dispersed after the Civil War, find themselves on opposite sides of a final, deadly showdown.
Riding Wild is the old story of a range war between cattle barons and homesteaders.

Bill Elliott stops the evil cattle rustlers, who use up sheriffs like disposable razor blades. Instead of the customary gun battles, Elliott was known for his fisticuffs action and so he uses his knuckles to clean out the bad guys and win the heart of Iris Meredith, who had been the main lady for Charles Starrett in his westerns.
A tenderfoot Chicago hotel clerk is taken on a cattle-drive to Mexico by famous trail boss Tom Reece.

Zane Grey's novel "Twin Sombreros" is the inspiration behind this hard riding dust-up of a Western. Randolph Scott is the fast gun whose purpose is to cut a corrupt cattle baron down to size when the baron selfishly monopolizes the market.
An oil derrick owner stubbornly drills for oil despite the pressure from major oil companies to sell her land.

An action-packed, slapstick western tale which has Buck Weylan (Buck Jones) coming from Arizona to help Ann (Dorothy Fay), whose cattle are being snatched by an evil gang of rustlers. Jones mixes law and order with comedy and romance.
A gunslinger helps an ungrateful town fight off a raid by his former gang.
A drifter takes on marauding Apaches in order to save a group of besieged settlers.
